main.title: Battlefield 4
main.subtitle: Large multiplayer battles meet a changing battlefield
main.summary: Battlefield 4 is a 2013 first-person shooter game developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts. The game was released in October and November for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. It is the thirteenth installment in the Battlefield series and is the sequel of 2011's Battlefield 3, taking place six years later during the fictional "War of 2020".

cards.heading: The next Battlefield reaches two console generations
cards.text:
Battlefield 4 is a 2013 first-person shooter game developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts. The game was released in October and November for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. It is the thirteenth installment in the Battlefield series and is the sequel of 2011's Battlefield 3, taking place six years later during the fictional "War of 2020".

Battlefield 4 was met with positive reception for its multiplayer mode, gameplay and graphics, but was criticized for its single-player campaign and for numerous bugs and glitches in the multiplayer. It was a commercial success, selling over seven million copies.

cards.heading: Commanding battles with up to 64 players
cards.text: Battlefield 4's multiplayer contains three playable factions—the United States, China, and Russia—fighting against each other, in up to 64-player matches on PC, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One (24-Player on Xbox 360 and PS3). A newly reintroduced "Commander Mode", last seen in Battlefield 2142, gives one player on each team a real-time strategy-like view of the entire map and the ability to give orders to teammates. Also, the Commander can observe the battle through the eyes of the players on the battlefield, deploying vehicle and weapon drops to "keep the war machinery going", and order in missile strikes on hostile targets. A spectator mode is included, enabling players to spectate others in first or third person, as well as use a free camera to pan around the map from any angle.

cards.heading: Levolution transforms the Siege of Shanghai
cards.text: On June 10, 2013, at E3, DICE featured the map "Siege of Shanghai", depicting the People's Liberation Army against the U.S. Marine Corps. The gameplay showcased Commander Mode; new weapons and vehicles; and the "Levolution" gameplay mechanic. The video displays the last of these at various points, including: a player destroying a support pillar to trap an enemy tank above it; and a large skyscraper (with an in-game objective on the top floor) collapsing in the center of the map, kicking up a massive dust cloud throughout the map and bringing the objective closer to ground level. Levolution also includes effects such as shooting a fire extinguisher to fill the room with obscuring clouds, car alarms going off when stepped on, metal detectors going off once passed through, or cutting the power in a room to reduce others' visibility.

main.title: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag
main.subtitle: Edward Kenway sails through the Golden Age of Piracy
main.summary: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: The sixth main Assassin?s Creed adventure
cards.text: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the sixth major installment in the Assassin's Creed series. Its historical timeframe precedes that of Assassin's Creed III (2012), but its modern-day sequences succeed III's own. Black Flag was originally released for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and Wii U in October 2013 and a month later for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One. It was later ported to the Nintendo Switch as part of The Rebel Collection alongside Assassin's Creed Rogue in December 2019. The game was released for Google Stadia in September 2021.

cards.heading: Edward Kenway and the struggle over the Observatory
cards.text: The plot is set in a fictional history of real-world events and follows the millennia-old struggle between the Assassins, who fight to preserve peace and free will, and the Templars, who desire peace through control. The framing story is set in the 21st century and depicts the player as an employee of Abstergo Entertainment (a company used as a front by the modern-day Templars), who is manipulated into uncovering secrets related to the Assassin–Templar conflict and the precursor race known as the First Civilization. The main story is set in the West Indies during the Golden Age of Piracy from 1715 to 1722, and follows notorious Welsh pirate Edward Kenway, grandfather of Assassin's Creed III protagonist Ratonhnhaké:ton / Connor and father of antagonist Haytham Kenway, as he searches for fortune and a mythical location called the Observatory, which is sought by both the Assassins and the Templars. A major plot element concerns the attempted establishment of an independent Pirate republic in the Caribbean.

cards.heading: Sailing, exploration and Freedom Cry
cards.text: Unlike previous games, gameplay elements focus more on the ship-based exploration of the seamless open world map, while also retaining the series' third-person land-based exploration, melee combat, and stealth system. Multiplayer also returns, albeit with only land-based modes and settings. The game's setting spans the West Indies with the three main cities of Havana, Nassau, and Kingston, along with numerous islands, sunken ships, and forts. Players have the option to harpoon large sea animals and hunt land animals. For the first time in the series, naval exploration is a major part of an Assassin's Creed game, where Edward captains the Jackdaw, a brig he captures from a Spanish fleet in an early game mission. A number of downloadable content (DLC) packs were released to support Black Flag, including Assassin's Creed Freedom Cry, a story expansion that was later made available as a standalone game in 2014. Set over a decade after Black Flag's main campaign, Freedom Cry follows Adéwalé, Edward's former quartermaster who became an Assassin.

cards.heading: Naval exploration earns critical acclaim
cards.text: Black Flag sold more than eleven million copies by 2014. Reviews praised its naval combat, exploration, characters and pirate setting, while criticising repetitive historical missions and aspects of the modern-day story. It won Best Action Adventure Game at the 2013 Spike VGX awards. Assassin's Creed Rogue and Unity followed in November 2014.

main.title: Call of Duty: Ghosts
main.subtitle: A new military story beyond the earlier subseries
main.summary: Call of Duty: Ghosts is a 2013 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision.

cards.heading: A new entry from Infinity Ward
cards.text: Call of Duty: Ghosts is a 2013 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision. It is the tenth major installment in the Call of Duty series and the sixth developed by Infinity Ward. It was released for PlayStation 3, Wii U, Windows, Xbox 360, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One in November 2013.

cards.heading: Campaign, Squads and Extinction
cards.text: The game acts as a standalone installment in the wider Call of Duty franchise in lieu of the World War II, Black Ops and Modern Warfare series that preceded it. Ghosts inherits much of the core gameplay and structure of previous titles, with a mission-based campaign and an open-ended multiplayer, though it has an increased focus on tactical gameplay, including the addition of new "Squads" modes and orbital strike superweapons to the multiplayer. The single-player campaign follows a protracted high-tech war against a dictatorial united South America. Ghosts also features an alternative co-operative shooter mode titled Extinction, acting as a spiritual successor to the Zombies co-operative PvE game modes introduced to the franchise in Call of Duty: World at War.

cards.heading: Critical reception across two generations
cards.text: Reviews were mixed. Critics welcomed parts of multiplayer and Extinction, but questioned the campaign and its reuse of familiar ideas. Its commercial performance fell short of Activision's expectations as the game launched across two console generations.

main.title: Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus
main.subtitle: One last journey for the Future saga
main.summary: Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, first released in Australia on 6 November 2013. A prisoner escort goes wrong, drawing the partners into a conflict involving dangerous beings from another dimension. The shorter adventure serves as an epilogue to the Future saga, returning to the established mixture of jumping, gadgets and extravagant weapons. Gravity provides its main variation, altering how a route is crossed and what direction a character can treat as the ground in a particular section.

cards.heading: One last journey for the Future saga
cards.text: Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, first released in Australia on 6 November 2013. A prisoner escort goes wrong, drawing the partners into a conflict involving dangerous beings from another dimension. The shorter adventure serves as an epilogue to the Future saga, returning to the established mixture of jumping, gadgets and extravagant weapons. Gravity provides its main variation, altering how a route is crossed and what direction a character can treat as the ground in a particular section.

cards.heading: Turn a different surface into a path
cards.text: Gravity-based gadgets allow Ratchet to reach places that would otherwise remain separated by empty space. The player reads the environment for possible connections rather than treating every gap as a jump. The arsenal also supplies comic new effects: the Winterizer turns enemies into snowmen, while the Nightmare Box distracts and frightens them. Such weapons change the character of a fight as well as dealing damage. Familiar improvements through use encourage another round with a newly obtained tool, even within a campaign built on a relatively compact scale.

cards.heading: Clank crosses the rift
cards.text: Clank's Netherverses use two-dimensional layouts where changing gravity directs movement through a maze. A pursuing Nether must be guided toward the required exit, making the route and its timing the main problem. These sequences give Clank a separate activity while supporting the dimensional danger in Ratchet's story. Michael Bross composed the music, and reviewers generally praised the presentation and controls while noting the short length. Released near the end of the PlayStation 3 generation, Into the Nexus closed this part of the partners' journey before their later PlayStation adventures.

main.title: XCOM: Enemy Within
main.subtitle: The expansion introduces genetic changes to soldiers
main.summary: XCOM: Enemy Within is an expansion pack for the turn-based tactical video game XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

cards.heading: New mechanics and genetic modifications
cards.text: XCOM: Enemy Within is an expansion pack for the turn-based tactical video game XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The expansion pack primarily adds new gameplay elements to the base game, as well as introducing new themes of transhumanism via aggressive gene therapy.

cards.heading: Releases across different platforms
cards.text: XCOM: Enemy Within was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360 in November 2013 and received generally favorable reviews from critics. In June 2014, Feral released both XCOM: Enemy Within and its base game XCOM: Enemy Unknown for Linux. The game also came to the iOS App Store and Google Play Store a year after the initial release, on November 12, 2014. On March 22, 2016, the game was released on the PlayStation Store for PlayStation Vita.

cards.heading: Expansion, Commander Edition and standalone versions
cards.text: The Windows, OS X and Linux editions require XCOM: Enemy Unknown to play; Enemy Within was released for Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 as part of the Commander Edition bundle with Enemy Unknown. The iOS and Android versions were released as stand-alone apps not requiring the original mobile port of Enemy Unknown to play. The PlayStation Vita version is only available bundled with Enemy Unknown under the title, XCOM: Enemy Unknown Plus.

main.title: PlayStation 4
main.subtitle: A moment worth sharing
main.summary: A new button on the controller made recording and sharing part of the console's everyday vocabulary.

cards.heading: Sharing play through the DualShock 4
cards.text: The DualShock 4 carried a small but revealing change: a dedicated sharing control. PlayStation 4 made capturing a surprising moment and showing it to someone else part of the console itself. Live streaming and, later, Share Play extended that idea. Playing a game and being an audience for a game were becoming closely connected experiences.

cards.heading: North America launches before Japan
cards.text: This was also the first PlayStation home console to reach North America before Japan. It launched there on 15 November 2013, followed by Europe on 29 November. The Japanese release came on 22 February 2014. Those regional dates are part of its history, rather than interchangeable labels for one global event.

cards.heading: The machine and its cultural legacy
cards.text: The original machine's sloping black case gave this increasingly social platform a compact physical form. Its library could still offer solitary journeys: Bloodborne, Horizon Zero Dawn and God of War sat alongside experiences built around sharing a world with others. The console's cultural footprint includes both the games people played and the clips, broadcasts and conversations that travelled beyond them.

main.title: Killzone Shadow Fall
main.subtitle: A Shadow Marshal and an OWL drone face a divided Vekta
main.summary: Killzone Shadow Fall is a 2013 first-person shooter developed by Guerrilla Games as a PlayStation 4 launch title. Shadow Marshal Lucas Kellan investigates a new threat on the divided planet Vekta.

cards.heading: A new generation and a divided Vekta
cards.text: Killzone Shadow Fall is a 2013 first-person shooter developed by Guerrilla Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment as a PlayStation 4 launch title. Set thirty years after Killzone 3, it follows Lucas Kellan, a Shadow Marshal investigating a new threat on Vekta. More open mission areas allow stealth and alternative routes, while multiplayer offers new weapon customisation options. The game uses Guerrilla's Decima engine.

cards.heading: The OWL drone expands the arsenal
cards.text: Like its predecessors, Shadow Fall is a first-person shooter in a science fiction setting. Staple weapons such as the M82 Assault Rifle, stA-52 Assault Rifle, and stA-18 pistol return from the earlier Killzone games, albeit in new forms and variations. New weapons include the LSR44, a recoil-free, hybrid assault/charge sniper rifle that functions much like a miniaturized rail-gun, and the OWL, an advanced hovering attack drone (used by the Shadow Marshals) that can attack/stun when it is adjacent to an adversary, as well as deploy an instant zip line, protect the player from enemy fire with an energy shield, and hack/scan terminals and enemy alarms to prevent reinforcements from arriving.

cards.heading: Open routes and stealth change the campaign
cards.text: More open levels give the player several ways to reach an objective, including stealth and direct combat. During much of the first half of the campaign, Kellan fights alone with support from the OWL drone. Later, Echo sometimes joins him and can snipe enemies marked by the player.

main.title: Need for Speed Rivals
main.subtitle: Ghost Games makes its Need for Speed debut
main.summary: Need for Speed Rivals is a 2013 racing video game developed in collaboration between Ghost Games and Criterion Games, and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: Ghost Games makes its Need for Speed debut
cards.text: Need for Speed Rivals is a 2013 racing game developed by Ghost Games with Criterion Games and published by Electronic Arts. The twentieth entry in the series was the debut project from Ghost Games, formerly EA Gothenburg.

cards.heading: Critical reception and the closure of online services
cards.text: Rivals was well received by critics at E3 2013 and was awarded with "Best Racing Game" from Game Critics Awards. It received mostly positive reviews upon release. It was followed in 2015 by the mobile game Need for Speed: No Limits, and the self-titled reboot. The online services for Rivals shut down on 7 October 2025, though the game continues to be playable offline.

main.title: Resogun
main.subtitle: Rescue the last humans in a world built from voxels
main.summary: Resogun is a 2013 shoot 'em up video game developed by Housemarque and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 4. Ports for PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita developed by Climax Studios were released the following year. It draws heavily from the games Defender and Datastorm, and is considered the spiritual successor to Housemarque's previous shoot 'em up games Super Stardust HD and Super Stardust Delta.

cards.heading: An arcade shooter for the PlayStation 4 launch
cards.text: Resogun is a 2013 shoot 'em up video game developed by Housemarque and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 4. Ports for PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita developed by Climax Studios were released the following year. It draws heavily from the games Defender and Datastorm, and is considered the spiritual successor to Housemarque's previous shoot 'em up games Super Stardust HD and Super Stardust Delta.

cards.heading: Saving humans across five cylindrical worlds
cards.text: In Resogun, the player battles phases of enemies on five distinct, cylindrical, voxel-based levels: Acis, Ceres, Decima, Febris, and Mefitis. Each level is separated into three phases and includes a unique boss enemy. Although the primary goal of each level is to eliminate all enemies, including the boss, humans can be saved in order to gain a bonus score towards the player's final score. In order to save a human, it must first be released from its chamber by killing a set of "keepers." Upon release, the player can pick up the human and bring it to one of two safety points.

cards.heading: Three ships, Overdrive and nova-bombs
cards.text: Three ships (Nemesis, Ferox, and Phobos) are available for selection; each ship has different levels of agility, boost, and overdrive. In addition, various upgrades and powerups are available to the player throughout each level. Overdrive, once charged, produces a powerful beam of energy that is capable of taking out large quantities of enemies. Boost acts as a speed boost and allows the player to escape from enemies, as well as destroy enemies by colliding with them. The nova-bomb produces a large explosion that clears all enemies currently on the level. These are limited in quantity but can be obtained through pickups. Ship upgrades and extra lives can also be obtained through pickups, or by saving humans. You can also choose from a selection of custom made skins for your ship made by other people online.

main.title: Tearaway
main.subtitle: A message through the paper
main.summary: The screen becomes a meeting place between a folded world and the hands holding it.

cards.heading: A messenger addressed to you
cards.text: Tearaway first reached PS Vita players in Australia and New Zealand on November 20, 2013, followed by Europe and North America on November 22. Media Molecule’s messenger, iota or atoi, carries a delivery intended for the player. The handheld is part of that relationship: fingers appear through the paper world using the rear touch panel, while the camera, microphone and touch screen connect physical actions to the journey.

cards.heading: Paper that leaves the screen
cards.text: The paper is more than a surface treatment. Photographing colourless objects restores their appearance and unlocks printable models, extending the adventure into cutting, folding and glue. The original photo interface and publisher artwork show that exchange between player and world. Kenneth Young and Brian D’Oliveira’s folk-inflected score gives it a handmade musical character. The later PlayStation 4 adaptation, Tearaway Unfolded, reworks the idea for a different controller; it does not replace the original Vita release.
